title: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head W (Ministry of Transport)

sections.label: COVID-19 support for point-to-point drivers
sections.summary: 300,000 surgical masks and a S$77 million Point-to-Point Support Package with three components were provided to taxi and private hire car drivers affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: To better protect our taxi and private hire car drivers from COVID-19, 300,000 surgical masks have been provided for them to offer to passengers who are unwell.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Point-to-Point Support Package totaling S$77 million dollars was announced to support our drivers whose livelihoods have been adversely affected by the virus outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: There are three components: the Special Relief Fund (SRF), the Government and NTUC Driver Care Fund for drivers and the Waiver of the Operator Licence Fee for Point-to-Point Transport Operators.

sections.label: North-South and East-West lines renewal
sections.summary: Minister Khaw Boon Wan announced the multi-year renewal of the North-South and East-West lines will cost more than S$2.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan had recently announced that the multi-year programme to renew the North-South and East-West lines, which are Singapore’s oldest and most heavily used lines, will cost more than S$2.5 billion dollars.

sections.label: Cross Island Line and rail network
sections.summary: When the Cross Island Line is completed, scheduled for 2031, Singapore will have doubled its rail network to 360 km.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Once the Cross Island Line is completed – currently scheduled for 2031 –Singapore will have doubled its rail network to 360 km.

sections.label: Sustainable rail reliability and operating costs
sections.summary: The speaker notes large 2019 losses by SMRT Trains and SBS Transit and invites the Minister to share long term strategic plans for sustaining rail reliability and service levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The operating costs of maintaining rail reliability at current levels need to be sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The large losses recorded by both SMRT Trains and SBS Transit reported in 2019 provides us with an insight of the costs involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I therefore invite the Minister to share with us the Ministry’s long term strategic plans on sustaining and securing Singapore’s future public rail transportation needs as the Government continues to invest in expanding and renewing our rail network, while concurrently maintaining current reliability and service levels.

sections.label: Special Relief Fund and rental rebates
sections.summary: P2P drivers appreciated the help compared to SARS, but the S$10 per day Special Relief Fund is not enough, and taxi operators top up with rental rebates of up to S$26.50 per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Such move was greatly appreciated by the P2P drivers, because it is such a big improvement as compared to the time of SARS, when the help was given later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, the Special Relief Fund (SRF) of $10 per day is really not enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Taxi operators have provided a top-up, by providing rental rebate of up to $26.50 per day, over and above the SRF of $10 per day.

sections.label: Point-to-point relief package for drivers
sections.summary: With tourist arrivals falling and cabbies reporting over 25% and private hire drivers over 30% earnings drops, LTA announced a S$77 million package giving about 40,000 eligible drivers S$20 per day per vehicle for three months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, with tourist arrivals plummeting and an increasingly number of companies allowing their staff to work from home to reduce the risk of infection, cabbies have reported a drop in earnings of over 25%, while private hire drivers have seen a drop of over 30%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To address this, LTA announced a $77 million point-to-point package to help taxis and private hire businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The relief package gives about 40,000 eligible drivers $20 per day per vehicle for three months to ride through this difficult time.

sections.label: Discretionary right turn accidents
sections.summary: A student with right-of-way was hit by a vehicle at a discretionary right turn, which the speaker says causes accidents because two green lights operate at once.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Fast forward to 2020, 6 January, to be precise, a student, with the right-of-way and hidden by a vehicle waiting at the discretionary right injunction was sent flying through the air by another vehicle who did not see the young man crossing the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The discretionary turning on green rule is the recipe for accidents to happen because there are two green lights in operation at the same time: one for the vehicle to turn right and the other for the pedestrians to cross.

sections.label: Pedestrian overhead bridges lifts
sections.summary: LTA announced that by 2022, 103 pedestrian overhead bridges will be retrofitted with lifts, about 19% of all POBs having lift access by next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: Last November, LTA announced that by 2022, 103 of them will be retrofitted with lifts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: That is about 19% of all POBs that will have lift access by next year.

sections.label: MRT operating cost deficit
sections.summary: The MRT system faces an operating cost deficit that will grow with new rail lines that may redistribute existing passengers rather than grow new ridership.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our MRT system is also facing an operating cost deficit which will grow with new rail lines that may well redistribute existing passengers rather than grow new ridership.

sections.label: Singapore regional air sea hub
sections.summary: Singapore is a regional air and sea transport hub, aided by Jewel at Changi and the Tuas container terminal relocation, but its status cannot be taken for granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore acts as a regional air and sea transport hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have managed to use Singapore's geographical location to our advantage, and over the years we have become a major regional and international hub through bold vision and thorough planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The opening of Jewel at Changi Airport has definitely upped the attractiveness of Changi as regional air hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We are also relocating our container terminal to Tuas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But our status as a regional air and sea hub cannot be taken for granted and there are many regional countries also eyeing the pie.

sections.label: Piracy incidents and Malacca Straits Patrol
sections.summary: Minister Khaw said there were 12 piracy and robbery incidents in December 2019 and January 2020, none in Singapore's territorial waters, and described the Malacca Straits Patrol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Khaw Boon Wan replied that there were 12 incidents involving piracy and robbery in December 2019 and January 2020, and as none of those incidents happened in our territorial waters, no investigations were required of our agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to him, the Republic of Singapore Navy conducts joint coordinated patrols with Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand through the Malacca Straits Patrol (MSP) in the Strait of Singapore as well as in the Strait of Malacca; that the MSP hold regular meetings to enhance coordination, review conduct of operations and share intelligence and information.

sections.label: No Singapore investigation into piracy
sections.summary: Minister Khaw's answer confirmed Singapore carried out no investigation into the reported piracy incidents, leaving the cause, spike and culprits unknown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister Khaw's answer confirmed that no investigation was carried out by Singapore on the incidents reported and we are none the wiser about the cause of these piracy incidents – why there was a sudden spike in the number or who were the culprits behind the incidents?

sections.label: E-scooter footpath ban, cycling paths
sections.summary: MOT announced in November 2019 that e-scooters will be banned from footpaths but allowed on cycling paths, with the network extended to 1,300 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MOT announced in November 2019 that e-scooters will be banned from footpaths but will be allowed on cycling paths; and MOT will extend the network of cycling path from 440 km to 1,300 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last month, at the Second Reading of the Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill, I had some questions on the proposed extension of the cycling path network.

sections.label: Reconsidering PMDs if paths costly
sections.summary: If linking cycling paths between homes and offices seems too expensive, impractical or ambitious, MOT may have to reconsider e-scooters, other PMDs and e-bikes for first and final mile connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: On the other hand, if the extensive linkage between cycling paths in our homes and offices seem too expensive, impractical or ambitious, then MOT may have to reconsider e-scooters, other PMDs and even e-bikes as a serious option for first and final mile connectivity.

sections.label: Food delivery companies' rider safety
sections.summary: MOT affirmed food delivery companies should ensure their riders ride safely, and the speaker asks if these regulations will be in subsidiary legislation, suggesting penalties for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last month, in response to my Parliamentary Question, MOT affirmed that under the Active Mobility (Amendment) and the Shared Mobility Enterprises (Control and Licensing) Acts, food delivery companies should be responsible for ensuring that their riders ride safely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Minister confirm that these regulations will be included in the subsidiary legislation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, I would also like to suggest that such regulations must include imposition of penalties on the food delivery companies in the event of any failure on the part of their riders to comply with the law, for example, pertaining to the use of devices with correct specifications, use of devices on paths allowed for the relevant devices, riding safely, and so on.

sections.label: Third-party insurance for riders
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOT will ensure third party liability insurers cannot exclude or repudiate policy liability for accidents occurring while riders are in breach of the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Separately, in respect of the delivery companies’ obligations to ensure that their active mobility riders have third-party insurance, will MOT take steps to ensure that all third party liability insurers will not be able to exclude or repudiate policy liability for accidents which take place while the riders are in breach of the law?

sections.label: Funding for island-wide cycling network
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min mentioned early this year that the Government will spend more than $1 billion to accelerate completion of the island-wide cycling network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Chairman, early this year, Senior Minister of State Lam Pin Min mentioned that the Government will spend more than $1 billion to accelerate the completion of the island-wide cycling network.

sections.label: Accelerating cycling path network expansion
sections.summary: The speaker is glad MOT is accelerating construction of the cycling path network, previously announced to expand from 440 km to 750 km by 2025 and 1,300 km by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, I am glad that MOT is accelerating the construction of Singapore’s network of cycling paths by a few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It was previously announced that the network would be expanded from the 440 km currently, to 750 km by 2025, and up to 1,300 km by 2030.

sections.label: Overseas train services bidding
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister when LTA and Singapore train operators should jointly bid to manage train services overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to ask the Minister when is a good time for LTA and Singapore train operators to join forces to bid for management of train services overseas?

sections.label: Bukit Panjang and Sengkang-Punggol LRT
sections.summary: The Bukit Panjang LRT is undergoing a $344 million overhaul due in 2024, while parts of the Sengkang-Punggol LRT are reaching a critical lifespan point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Bukit Panjang LRT system, dogged by reliability issues, is now undergoing a $344 million overhaul that is due to be completed in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Yet, we should not forget that parts of the Sengkang-Punggol LRT system (SPLRT) are also reaching a critical point in their lifespan where concerns on reliability may begin to surface.

sections.label: Singapore rail network reliability
sections.summary: Reliability of Singapore's overall rail network improved steadily, reaching 1.08 million MKBF in the first nine months of 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Reliability of Singapore’s overall rail network has continued to improve steadily, reaching an impressive 1.08 million MKBF in the first nine months of 2019.

sections.label: PSA Tuas Mega Port
sections.summary: PSA Tuas Mega Port will start operations next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: PSA Tuas Mega Port will start operations next year.

sections.label: Worker travel time to Tuas
sections.summary: The complete journey excludes another half hour to the worker's Tuas Boulevard workplace, meaning 15 to 16 hours daily for work and travel on a 12-hour shift.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The complete journey does not factor in another half hour of travelling time to his actual workplace along Tuas Boulevard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This worker will be spending a minimum of 15 to 16 hours per day just for work and travel, assuming he is on a 12-hour shift roster.

sections.label: Proposed MRT line down-south
sections.summary: At last year's Committee of Supply debate, the speaker proposed an MRT line down-south, which MOT dismissed due to projected low ridership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At last year's Committee of Supply debate, I proposed to MOT to consider an MRT line down-south to reduce travelling time and the idea was dismissed due to projected low ridership.

sections.label: TEL worksite and langurs
sections.summary: The passage asks if TEL can finish before 2023 and states worksite A1W1 clearance threatens the 61 remaining Raffles' Banded Langurs, including four males needing that forest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Is it possible that completion of the TEL may take place earlier than 2023?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: People are concerned that the clearance and construction work at worksite A1W1 will have a major impact in breaking up wildlife habitats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It would mean that tree-dwelling animals like the Raffles' Banded Langurs might not be able to get from one forest patch to another and this will threaten their survival.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: There are only 61 Raffles' Banded Langurs left in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If the forest is cleared for the worksite, the Langurs who rely on tree canopies will be forced to come down to the ground to use the roads to cross and they will likely get injured or killed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We know through the work of Dr Andie Ang that a bachelor group of four male Langurs – Leonardo, Michelangelo, Donatello and Raphael – need the forest at the worksite A1W1.

sections.label: Moving worksite A1W1 to SICC
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOT will move worksite A1W1 into SICC to avoid impacting the langurs' forest, and notes MRT MKBF exceeded 1 million km from October 2018 to September 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOT consider moving worksite A1W1 further into Singapore Island Country Club (SICC) where the forest that the Langurs need will not be impacted?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The overall MRT Mean Km Between Failure (MKBF) was over 1 million km from October 2018 to September 2019.

sections.label: Phasing out combustion engine vehicles
sections.summary: The passage states the Government's push to phase out internal combustion engine vehicles by 2040 means over 600,000 diesel and petrol vehicles today will be replaced in 20 years unless the vehicle population shrinks drastically.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Chairman, the push by the Government to phase out the internal combustion engine vehicles in Singapore by 2040 is a very ambitious plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: This means that more than 600,000 diesel and petrol vehicles today will be replaced by full electric vehicles or other green vehicles in 20 years' time unless the Government is thinking of shrinking the vehicle population very drastically.

sections.label: Electric vehicles and charging points
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore today has about 1,125 electric vehicles supported by 1,600 charging points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: Today, we have about 1,125 electric vehicles (EVs) supported by 1,600 charging points.

sections.label: VES and EEAI rebate caps
sections.summary: The passage states the Vehicular Emissions Scheme gives fleet owners up to $30,000 rebate off the Additional Registration Fee, while the EV Early Adoption Incentive is capped at $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: The current Vehicular Emissions Scheme (VES) allows fleet owner to enjoy up to $30,000 of rebate off the Additional Registration Fee (ARF) but the EV Early Adoption Incentive (EEAI) is only capped at $20,000 rebate off the ARF.

sections.label: SP Group charging network commitment
sections.summary: The passage states SP Group has committed to operate a public charging network with 1,000 charging points by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: SP Group has committed to operate a public charging network with 1,000 charging points by 2020.

sections.label: RTS link peak hour commuters
sections.summary: The RTS link will allow 60,000 additional commuters to cross the Causeway during peak hour when ready.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: When ready, the RTS link will allow 60,000 additional commuters to cross the Causeway during peak hour.

sections.label: Flight cancellations and Changi passenger volume
sections.summary: Airlines cancelled over 20% of scheduled flights, and Changi passenger volume plunged by 25% and may fall further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Airlines have cancelled over 20% of their scheduled flights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Passenger volume at Changi has plunged by 25% and is likely to fall further.

sections.label: Fall in transport ridership
sections.summary: Bus, rail, taxi and private hire car riderships fell by about 20% along with reduced tourist arrivals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Along with reduced tourist arrivals, our bus, rail, taxi and private hire car riderships have fallen by about 20%.

sections.label: Project suspension until April
sections.summary: The project remains suspended until the end of April this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: The project remains suspended until the end of April this year.

sections.label: Speeding up cycling and road projects
sections.summary: Over $100 million worth of cycling path and road construction projects can be sped up by up to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: On the domestic land transport side, we stand ready to speed up over $100 million worth of cycling path and road construction projects by up to three years.

sections.label: North East and Downtown Line extensions
sections.summary: Extensions to the North East Line and Downtown Line will be completed by 2023 and 2024 respectively, within the next term of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Second, we will be completing the extensions to the North East Line and Downtown Line by 2023 and 2024 respectively – within the next term of Government.

sections.label: Keppel MRT stretch completion
sections.summary: The final Keppel stretch is the most challenging and costly to build, but on completion in 2025 it will raise MRT network resilience and commuter experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: This final stretch at Keppel is the most challenging to build and also the most costly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But when completed in 2025, it will significantly raise the resilience of our MRT network and the travelling experience of our commuters.

sections.label: Cross Island Line Phase 1
sections.summary: Phase 1 of the Cross Island Line will be completed by 2029, contributing to rail network growth to 360 km from 230 km.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Fifth, we will be completing Phase 1 of the Cross Island Line by 2029.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: This will contribute towards the subsequent growth of our rail network to 360 km from the current 230 km.

sections.label: Rail network and NSEWL renewal
sections.summary: By 2030 around 80% of Singaporeans will live within walking distance of a train station, and NSEWL renewal will be completed by around 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Indeed, by 2030, around 80% of Singaporeans will live within walking distance of a train station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: As Mr Cedric Foo remarked to me about our plan: “This is our commitment to build a liveable city in Singapore and this is MOT’s contribution to reducing traffic jams as well as carbon emissions!” Apart from expanding our rail network, we will finally complete the renewal of the North-South Line and East-West Lines (NSEWL) by around 2023.

sections.label: Transitional voucher for affected commuters
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira raised a transitional voucher idea; the speaker is unsure it is easy to design, cites cheaper off-peak rates, and says affected commuters will have reasonable travel alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira raised the idea of a transitional voucher for commuters affected by such optimisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: I am not so sure if it is easy to design such a scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But in a way, our cheaper off-peak rates are one such idea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: In any case, we always ensure that commuters affected will have reasonable travel alternatives so that they will not be left in the lurch, and our Members do understand the need for cost management.

sections.label: LTA evaluating request
sections.summary: LTA will evaluate his request seriously, carefully and fairly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: LTA will evaluate his request seriously, carefully and fairly.

sections.label: Completing $60 billion rail plan
sections.summary: The speaker says they are far from perfect and still have much to do, including completing the $60 billion strategic long-term plan for the rail network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: But we know we are far from perfect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
sentences.text: We still have a lot of things to do, including to complete the $60 billion strategic long-term plan for our rail network which I have outlined earlier and I look forward to Members’ continuing support.

sections.label: Aviation and maritime sector assistance
sections.summary: A $112 million package helps the aviation sector, and passenger vessels get a 50% port dues concession.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: On top of economy-wide measures, we have rolled out a $112 million assistance package to help the aviation sector defray cost and ease cashflow pressures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: For the maritime sector, we have provided a 50% port dues concession to passenger vessels, on top of all existing concessions.

sections.label: SIA Group flight suspensions
sections.summary: COVID-19 led the SIA Group to temporarily suspend over 9,000 flights, nearly 15% of scheduled flights from February to end-May.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Due to the adverse impact of COVID-19, the SIA Group has temporarily suspended more than 9,000 flights, or nearly 15% of all its scheduled flights from February to end of May.

sections.label: Aviation Development Fund extension
sections.summary: CAAS will extend the $280 million Aviation Development Fund for another five years, from 2020 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Take, for example, CAAS will extend the $280 million Aviation Development Fund for another five years, from 2020 to 2025.

sections.label: New Work-Study Diploma courses
sections.summary: With ITE, two new Work-Study Diploma courses in Airport Operations and Maritime Business Management will launch in April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Come April, together with ITE, we will launch two new Work-Study Diploma courses in Airport Operations and Maritime Business Management respectively.

sections.label: Malacca Straits Patrol piracy collaboration
sections.summary: Piracy in the Strait of Singapore requires regional collaboration, so the Malacca Straits Patrol involves Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: However, as the Strait of Singapore does not only include Singapore territorial waters, the fight against piracy and armed robbery requires strong collaboration among all regional partners and Singapore cannot tackle it alone.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: This is why there is the Malacca Straits Patrol (MSP) involving our military and the militaries of Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The MSP includes air and sea patrols in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: And as the Minister for Defence had shared with the House during MINDEF's COS debates on Monday, MINDEF has reached out to its counterparts in Malaysia and Indonesia to propose that MSP be extended to other areas in our surrounding waters.

sections.label: Singapore joining CORSIA voluntary phase
sections.summary: Singapore is ready to participate in the voluntary phase of CORSIA, which starts next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: First, Singapore is ready to participate in the voluntary phase of the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) that starts next year.

sections.label: IMO 2020 sulphur fuel regulation
sections.summary: On 1 January 2020 Singapore and the world implemented the IMO 2020 regulation cutting vessel fuel sulphur content from 3.5% to 0.5% outside designated Emission Control Areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: On 1 January 2020, Singapore, together with the rest of the world, implemented the IMO 2020 regulation that reduces the permitted sulphur content in the fuels used by vessels from 3.5% to 0.5% outside designated Emission Control Areas.

sections.label: Maritime GreenFuture Fund and panel
sections.summary: The panel convenes first in April, and MPA and partners will set aside $40 million under the Maritime GreenFuture Fund for low-carbon technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The panel will convene for the first time in April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: And third, MPA and its partners will set aside $40 million under the Maritime GreenFuture Fund to be used for the research, test-bedding and adoption of low-carbon technologies.

sections.label: Islandwide Cycling Network investment
sections.summary: The Government plans to invest over $1 billion under the Islandwide Cycling Network programme, bringing 800 km of cycling paths forward to 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We have previously announced that there would be 750 km of cycling paths by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We will bring this milestone forward by two years, reaching 800 km of cycling paths by 2023, which is not that far away – about three years away.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: The Government plans to invest over $1 billion as part of the Islandwide Cycling Network (ICN) programme to bring the cycling path network closer to Singaporeans' doorsteps.

sections.label: Cycling path network by 2026
sections.summary: By 2026, Singapore's cycling path network will be expanded to 1,000 km.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: By 2026, Singapore's cycling path network will be expanded to 1,000 km.

sections.label: Cycling path network by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, the cycling path network would have been trebled to 1,320 km.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: By 2030, we would have trebled the cycling path network to 1,320 km.

sections.label: Routes for residents before 2030
sections.summary: Residents in Queenstown, Geylang, Jurong West, Sembawang, Yishun and Ang Mo Kio can rely on listed routes for journeys to the city before 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: In addition, residents in Queenstown, Geylang, Jurong West, Sembawang, Yishun and Ang Mo Kio can rely on the Queenstown-City and Geylang-City routes, the Round Island Route, and North-South Corridor for journeys from their homes to the city before 2030.

sections.label: SICC worksite and transport resilience
sections.summary: LTA is discussing optimising the worksite near SICC and using its non-playing areas, while transport sectors keep investing for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Concerning the proposed worksite near the Singapore Island Country Club (SICC) that Mr Louis Ng mentioned, LTA is committed to exploring how the worksite's footprint can be optimised and is in discussions with SICC to make use of its non-playing areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, we will stay resilient in this challenging period of COVID-19 and together, we will weather this storm.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: As Mr Yee Chia Hsing said, we did not become a major international aviation and maritime hub by chance, but through having a bold vision and thorough planning.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
sentences.text: We will continue to invest for the future, and sow the seeds for sustainable and competitive transport sectors.

sections.label: Fall in transport ridership
sections.summary: Ridership on MRT, public buses and point-to-point transport has fallen by around 20% compared to about a month ago.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Compared to about a month ago, ridership on our MRT, our public buses and point-to-point transport sector has fallen by around 20%.

sections.label: Point-to-Point Support Package
sections.summary: A $77 million package helps about 40,000 eligible drivers, with operator rebates bringing total support to over $90 million over three months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Together with the operators and the driver associations, we launched a $77 million Point-to-Point Support Package last month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This will help to partially defray business costs incurred by about 40,000 eligible drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Taxi operators such as ComfortDelGro, SMRT, TransCab and Premier have committed to further help and will lean forward to provide additional rental rebates to their drivers, on top of matching Government's contributions to the package.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This brings the total support committed by Government and operators to over $90 million over three months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Eligible drivers have started receiving rental rebates or cash grants of up to $36.50 per day.

sections.label: Cleaner energy vehicles by 2040
sections.summary: All vehicles will run on cleaner energy by 2040, meaning no new internal combustion engine vehicle purchases after 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As mentioned in Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat's Budget speech, all vehicles will run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This means that after 2030, we should see no new purchases of internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.

sections.label: EV upfront cost difference
sections.summary: The upfront cost of EVs is about 78% higher than equivalent ICE vehicles today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Today, the upfront cost of EVs is about 78% higher than equivalent ICE vehicles.

sections.label: Narrowing EV cost difference
sections.summary: The upfront cost difference between an EV and an equivalent ICE vehicle will be narrowed by up to $20,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: With this, the upfront cost difference between an EV and an equivalent ICE vehicle will be narrowed by up to $20,000.

sections.label: Cleaner energy public buses
sections.summary: All new public bus purchases will be cleaner energy buses, including electric or hybrid, towards all buses and taxis running on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Last year, I shared that all public buses and taxis will run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will go a step further: all new public bus purchases from now on will be cleaner energy buses, including electric or hybrid buses.

sections.label: Electric motorcycles and EV charging
sections.summary: High-powered e-motorcycles will be allowed into Singapore from 1 April 2020, and CHAdeMO, a fast EV charging method, will be approved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As one example, we will allow high-powered e-motorcycles into Singapore from 1 April 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Motorcyclists can now do their part for the environment by choosing an electric model.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We will also approve CHAdeMO; it is a fast charging method for EVs, an optional EV public charging standard.

sections.label: Autonomous vehicle public road trials
sections.summary: About 30 AVs are authorised for public road trials in a testbed expanded to include areas such as NUS and Jurong Island.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Today, about 30 AVs are authorised for public road trials in a testbed that has expanded to include areas such as the National University of Singapore and Jurong Island.

sections.label: AV bus captain training roadmap
sections.summary: LTA will work with NTWU and Public Transport Operators to develop a skills and training roadmap for AV buses, launched by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To further prepare our bus captains for AV buses, LTA will work with stakeholders such as NTWU and Public Transport Operators (PTOs) to develop a skills and training roadmap to be launched by the end of this year.

sections.label: Rail operator training incentives
sections.summary: Incentives will help rail operators expand training in data analytics and condition-based maintenance, with over 3,000 workers expected to benefit over five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: A key component of this is a set of incentives for rail operators to expand and accelerate their training in key technologies and skillsets such as data analytics and condition-based maintenance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We expect the first batch of workers to start training in these areas from the second quarter of this year, with over 3,000 expected to benefit over five years.

sections.label: Driver digital skills training
sections.summary: About 4,600 ComfortDelGro taxi drivers completed SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace training, and other driver training schemes are available.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For example, as of the end of 2019, about 4,600 ComfortDelGro taxi drivers have completed the SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace training programme, learning new skills to use e-payment technologies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, Grab and National Private Hire Vehicle Association (NPHVA) also launched the Grab Driver-Partner Training Kit that includes courses on safety and digital skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Over the next three months, drivers can also benefit from the Self-employed Persons (SEPs) Training Support Scheme, which the Minister for Manpower had announced in this House earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, Mr Chairman, we have three major strategies today to move towards the land transport system of the future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We emphasise "Walk-Cycle-Ride" to deliver on the vision that we have for a 45-minute city and 20-minute towns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We want the system to be clean and green, and for every part of the system to be optimised through the use of technology and across all of these strategies, throughout all of our efforts, we have to keep our focus on making sure that there are good jobs, that we look after the workers and we provide them the opportunities to retrain and re-skill themselves, to take advantage of these new opportunities.

sections.label: Transport safety and inclusivity investment
sections.summary: About $200 million was invested over five years on transport initiatives, with RAG arrows at over 300 junctions, targeting 1,200 by 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, we have invested about $200 million on various safety and inclusivity-related transport initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Mr Png Eng Huat will be pleased to know that we have implemented these RAG arrows at more than 300 junctions and target to have the arrows at a total of 1,200 junctions by 2023.

sections.label: Elderly taxi drivers licence renewal
sections.summary: By end of this year, elderly taxi drivers who passed TDVL medical exams can use them to renew Class 3 personal driving licences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: As shared in the House last week, by the end of this year, elderly taxi drivers who have passed the medical examinations for their Taxi Driver Vocational License (TDVL) can use them to renew their Class 3 personal driving licences.

sections.label: Silver Zones elderly accident reduction
sections.summary: Elderly accidents fell almost 80% in Silver Zones over six years, and plans continue for 50 Silver Zones island-wide by 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Over the past six years, accidents involving the elderly have reduced by almost 80% within these Silver Zones.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: With these encouraging results, we will continue with our plans to build a total of 50 Silver Zones island-wide by 2023.

sections.label: Caring SG Commuters Committee
sections.summary: The Public Transport Council set up a new Caring SG Commuters Committee to galvanise commuters and stakeholders, first facilitating awareness of commuters' challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: We can harness these individual acts of care into a national movement and build a culture where showing care for fellow commuters becomes a way of life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Hence, to galvanise commuters and other key stakeholders into action, the Public Transport Council has set up a new Caring SG Commuters Committee to help grow this movement: Firstly, the Committee will help to facilitate greater awareness of the challenges faced by commuters and show commuters how to care for others.

sections.label: Committee report to Transport Minister
sections.summary: The Committee will submit a report to the Minister for Transport in a year on findings and recommendations for a caring commuting culture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: The Committee will submit a report to the Minister for Transport in a year's time on its findings and recommendations on how we can continue to work with commuters and other stakeholders to build and sustain a caring commuting culture in Singapore.

sections.label: SMRT taxi booster seat pilot
sections.summary: SMRT will pilot providing booster seats in all its taxis at no additional charge to commuters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Today, I am pleased to announce that SMRT will be leaning forward to pilot the provision of booster seats in all its taxis, at no additional charge to commuters.

sections.label: Grab and Gojek drivers
sections.summary: Grab and Gojek rallied their drivers to provide on-demand transport services for healthcare professionals during the crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: For example, Grab and Gojek have rallied their drivers to step up in this time of crisis to provide on-demand transport services for our healthcare professionals.

sections.label: Air transport training package
sections.summary: An enhanced training and support package was announced, with SIA Group taking about 6,000 training places and up to 8,000 air transport workers benefiting.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The announcement of this enhanced training and support package was just made less than a week ago, on Monday.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Definitely, we will be working with SSG, e2i, WSG, CAAS and NTUC to see how we can jump-start some of these training courses for the air transport industry, especially the cabin crew that Mr Ang Hin Kee asked about in his cut.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: I would also like to update Mr Ang that the SIA Group, for example, will be taking up around 6,000 training places under this enhanced training and support package.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: And we understand that this package will benefit up to 8,000 air transport workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: And SIA Group also planned to schedule the crew for training, hopefully from April onwards, taking into consideration things like the network and rostering requirements.

sections.label: CRL Phase 2 station alignment
sections.summary: LTA engaged an advanced engineering study consultant to look into the design of station alignment for CRL Phase 2, including optimising the A1W1 worksite.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In fact, post-announcement, LTA has already engaged has already engaged the advanced engineering study consultant to look into the design of the alignment of the stations for CRL Phase 2 and that includes the optimisation of the worksite at A1W1.

sections.label: Cross Island Line environmental study
sections.summary: LTA engaged an environmental impact study sub-consultant and primate specialist Dr Andie Ang to study Cross Island Line Phase 2's impact on key biodiversity areas.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: At the same time, we have also engaged an environmental impact study sub-consultant who will work with the advanced engineering study consultant to study the environmental impact of Cross Island Line Phase 2 on key biodiversity areas along its alignment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: LTA has also enlisted the help of our local primate specialist, Dr Andie Ang – we all know her very well – to study these together with the EIS consultant.

sections.label: Electrification of private sector buses
sections.summary: Changes around vehicle emission schemes would be a key measure to incentivise private sector buses to transition to electric platforms.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For the electrification of private sector buses, the changes around vehicle emission schemes would be one of the key measures through which we hope they would be incentivised to then think about transition to electric platforms.

sections.label: Electric vehicle adoption targets
sections.summary: The speaker said there is time to meet targets but incentives are needed, and prefers a five-year target over a 10-year mark.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we do have some time to do it to meet our targets, but we will find ways to incentivise and encourage them to develop the skills and ability to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: I hear from Senior Minister of State Janil that in 10 years' time, almost 100% of the new cars sold will be electric vehicles or clean energy vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: Like I have mentioned in our Budget speech, I think we need a five-year target rather than shoot for a 10-year mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: If in five years, we are not even hitting 5%, I think we will miss our target.

sections.label: Electric vehicle cost strategies
sections.summary: The four moves aim to reduce the cost gap between electric and internal combustion vehicles and encourage consumer adoption.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, indeed our strategies that I have discussed – the four moves – are to reduce the cost differential between an electric vehicle and an internal combustion engine vehicle, encourage consumers to take this up as a choice, both because of the aspiration to be cleaner and greener, then hopefully it makes increasing economic sense to do so.
